CryptMsgEncodeAndSignCTL: dwFlags other than 0 is CMSG_CMS_ENCAPSULATED_CTL_FLAG only (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-cryptmsgsignctl: 'to encode a CMS compatible V3 SignedData message'); that needs the CMS encapsulation of the CTL in an OCTET STRING in CryptMsgOpenToEncode (CMSG_CMS_ENCAPSULATED_CONTENT_FLAG, absent from msg.c) and the page does not say what the signature covers; no Wine test; producing a message a Windows verifier may reject is worse than failing, so it still fails (FALSE) with the FIXME

patch 5060: IAsyncInfo::get_Id returns S_OK until Closed and E_ILLEGAL_METHOD_CALL after, as Windows' crypto.c:98-103 checks; the id is 1 (also cryptowinrt): the winrt-api page windows.foundation/iasyncinfo_id.md says only 'Gets the handle of the asynchronous operation', and no Windows test asserts a value or uniqueness, so no per-operation counter was added

wintrust CRYPT_GetLen with an indefinite-length (0x80) first length byte: SPC_* decoders in wintrust are not documented to accept BER indefinite lengths (learn.microsoft.com wintrust constants pages say nothing), no Wine or Windows test feeds one, and crypt32's decoder (which does) is a different code path; failing with CRYPT_E_ASN1_CORRUPT is the safe answer

WINTRUST_AddSgnr(fCounterSigner=TRUE): CRYPT_PROVIDER_SGNR page documents csCounterSigners/pasCounterSigners but no page or test says which array idxSigner selects or where the counter signer goes; no caller exists in Wine (softpub.c:1056 FIXME is the verification side). Also noticed, not changed: the insert at idxSigner < csSigners does memmove(&[idx], &[idx+1]) (shifts down, reads one element past the data), while the existing test only covers idx == csSigners and a todo_wine 'index ignored' case, so the intended Windows behaviour for a middle insert is unknown

WINTRUST_AddCert(fCounterSigner=TRUE, idxCounterSigner): same as 768, the natural reading (cert chain of pasSigners[idxSigner].pasCounterSigners[idxCounterSigner]) is not stated by any page and no Wine/Windows test exercises it

CryptDecodeObjectEx with struct types 4, 10, 11, 21, 39, 40, 41, 43, 44, 45, 47, 53, 58, 64, OCSP_RESPONSE...: the MS pages give the C structure but not what it maps to (PKCS_PRIVATE_KEY_INFO PrivateKey: the OCTET STRING contents or the whole element? absent algorithm parameters and absent attributes? X509_DSS_SIGNATURE byte order?), no Wine test exists for any of them, and RFC 5208/2986 fix the DER but not Windows' struct mapping; guessing would give callers wrong keys silently, so the FIXME and FALSE stay

CRYPT_GetBuiltinEncoder: the encoder side of the same struct types as index 25 (PKCS_PRIVATE_KEY_INFO, PKCS_ENCRYPTED_PRIVATE_KEY_INFO, X509_CERT_REQUEST_TO_BE_SIGNED, X509_KEYGEN_REQUEST_TO_BE_SIGNED, X509_DSS_PARAMETERS/SIGNATURE, X509_CERT_PAIR ...); same missing mapping details and no tests, so the FIXME stays

key_symmetric_encrypt, GCM with BCRYPT_AUTH_MODE_CHAIN_CALLS_FLAG: the BCRYPT_AUTHENTICATED_CIPHER_MODE_INFO page says the flags and cbAAD/cbData are 'maintained internally' (written back into the caller's struct) and pbMacContext is opaque, but not whether the AAD is passed on every chained call or only the first, whether chunks must be block aligned, or what is returned in pbTag on a chained call; Wine's bcrypt tests have no chained case; a wrong guess corrupts the tag silently, so it still fails with STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED
